scope: Only ancestor-task assignment freshness and drift-symlink reconciliation; no integration.

findings.body: Advancing an upstream task does not fence its existing receipt here. For example, after sealing CMAD1 at revision 1 and assigning CMAD1 revision 2, a currently authorized CMAD2 submission can still use the revision-1 predecessor: these checks only compare policy/epoch and artifact bytes, and neither discovery nor assignment advancement invalidates that receipt. This lets downstream stages seal against superseded task evidence. Check each ancestor's recorded principal/revision against its current host_tasks assignment before accepting it.

Resolving the path here removes symlink components before the guarded reader can reject them. An artifact replaced by an in-scope symlink is rejected by `digest_file(original_path, root)`, but `source_changed` returns `True`; a dangling in-scope symlink also returns `True`. Consequently, reopening can accept these paths and persist invalidations despite the newly enforced symlink-denial policy. Pass the original path to the guarded reader and recognize missing-source drift only when its underlying failure is `FileNotFoundError`, preserving scope denials for symlinks.
